recruitment_process_overview: Round 1: Behavioral (Psychometric) Assessment + Cognitive Gamified Assessment
Round 3: Communication Assessment (non-elimination in most drives)
Final: Technical Interview + HR Interview (sometimes combined panel)
Note: All assessment rounds are elimination rounds with sectional cut-offs; coding round is mandatory and its score counts toward final interview

rounds.type: Scenario-based personality questions with Agree/Disagree options
Logical brain games / puzzles (replaces old Quant+LR+English)
1 DSA problem + 1 SQL query + 1 UI (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) task

legacy_pre2025_pattern_cocubes.note: Still used in some drives; replaced in most 2025-2026 drives

syllabus_by_section.description: Personality/behavioral evaluation. No technical content. Consistency of answers matters.
Series of brain games replacing the traditional Quantitative Aptitude / Logical Reasoning / English sections. Evaluates logical and problem-solving ability in real time.
topics: Grid puzzles - pathfinding in minimum steps

syllabus_by_section.status: LEGACY (marked 'Not Asked Anymore' in the 2026 gamified pattern; still relevant for drives using the legacy pattern)
syllabus_by_section.description: 17 questions in legacy pattern. Tests grammar, vocabulary, comprehension.
topics: Speech and Tenses (Active/Passive Voice, Tense usage)
Fill in the blanks / Sentence Completion

syllabus_by_section.status: LEGACY (18 questions in legacy pattern; replaced by gamified cognitive in 2026)
LEGACY (15 questions in legacy pattern; replaced by gamified cognitive in 2026)
LEGACY - DROPPED from the 2025+ pattern (candidates reported 'no Quant' in the new technical round); still appears in some drives and in candidate prep material
syllabus_by_section.description: Numerical speed and accuracy. Moderate difficulty, no negative marking.
12 questions in legacy pattern; 0-8 in topic-wise analysis. Tests practical software literacy.
topics: MS Word: creating, editing, saving and printing text documents
MS Word: font and paragraph formatting
MS Word: inserting tables, smart art, page breaks
MS Word: spelling and grammar check
MS Excel: spreadsheet basics (create, edit, save, print)
MS Excel: working with functions & formulas
MS Excel: modifying worksheets with color & autoformats
MS Excel: graphically representing data - charts & graphs
MS Excel: data forms, data entry
MS Excel: data menu, subtotal, filtering data
MS PowerPoint: opening, viewing, creating and printing slides

syllabus_by_section.status: Current - both patterns (HIGH priority; 0-5 questions, high difficulty per PrepInsta analysis)
syllabus_by_section.description: Trace and predict output of pseudocode. 2025+ drives report heavy bit manipulation and bitwise operations, calculation-heavy, NO pen/paper allowed.
topics: Bitwise operators (AND, OR, XOR, shifts) - HIGH FREQUENCY

syllabus_by_section.status: Current - both patterns (10 questions legacy; HIGH priority in 2026)
topics: Cryptography and Network Security (encryption standards & algorithms)

syllabus_by_section.section: 10. Core CS Subjects (reported in 2025+ technical round)
syllabus_by_section.description: 2025 candidate reports: 'Python OOPs, Java OOPs, JavaScript frontend questions' + technical MCQs on OOPs, DBMS, OS, CN, SQL. MockStep lists these as high-priority.
topics: Object-Oriented Programming (OOPs) - Python and Java focused
Computer Fundamentals (0-5 questions per PrepInsta topic-wise analysis)

syllabus_by_section.status: Current - pattern changed from 2 questions to 3 questions (DSA + SQL + UI)
syllabus_by_section.description: Mandatory elimination round; score counts toward final interview. Graded on sample + hidden test cases. Clearing = passing all test cases on at least one problem.

current_3_problem_structure.examples: Array-based question (e.g. Rat Count House, Valid Password, Large-Small Sum, Array Rotation)
Create colored boxes or a basic UI element

difficulty_levels.beginner: Loops, conditionals, basic functions, number base conversion, logic/math warm-ups
difficulty_levels.medium: DS fundamentals + sorting/searching/recursion; may include DP and backtracking
difficulty_levels.hard: Complex algorithms, system design, OOP - less common, for advanced roles or tie-breakers

rules_and_marking: Scored by number of test cases passed
Clear = pass all test cases on at least one question
Partial credit for some test cases on another question
Write entire code from scratch (no pre-written code)

syllabus_by_section.status: Current - generally NOT an elimination round
syllabus_by_section.description: Tests English communication: sentence mastery, vocabulary, fluency, pronunciation. In 2025+ drives: 65 questions in 30 minutes.

focus: Final year project discussion (name, role, languages, contribution, issues faced)
Willingness to work in any business unit/service line

high_frequency_topics_2026: Python OOPs and Java OOPs (NEW emphasis, 2025+)

eligibility_criteria.academic_criteria: Minimum 60% aggregate (or 6.0 CGPA) from Class 10 through graduation
eligibility_criteria.backlogs: No active backlogs at application or onboarding
eligibility_criteria.education_gap: Up to 24 months acceptable with valid documentation
eligibility_criteria.reapplication_wait: Must not have attempted Accenture assessment in the last 3-6 months

emphasized_sections: Pseudo Code with bit manipulation (calculation-heavy, no pen/paper)
candidate_insights_2025_drive.coding_round_change: From 2 questions to 3: DSA (array) + SQL (JOINs on 2-3 tables) + JS frontend (UI element)
candidate_insights_2025_drive.exam_environment: Conducted offline in campus computer labs (anti-cheating) in reported drives
candidate_insights_2025_drive.tip: Prepare languages beyond C/C++: Python, Java, JS; practice mental bitwise tracing; revise SQL JOINs and basic HTML/CSS/JS

preparation_notes: No negative marking - attempt all questions
Sectional cut-offs apply; each round is elimination-based
Pseudocode sectional cut-off failure blocks the coding round
Practice previous-year questions: patterns repeat (Large-Small Sum, Array Rotation, Anagram, Binary Search)
Mock tests after basic prep; review mistakes
Consistency matters in the behavioral round
Revision of networking, cloud basics and OOP fundamentals is high-value
